stories.title: The beautiful game: revived art prize gives football its creative due once more | Emma John
summary: Football and the art world have long remained distant but the breadth of entries for this year’s award reveals a healthy revivalIt may be the Beautiful Game, but in its early decades football was a rare subject for artists.

In 1953 the Football Association launched an art prize, backed by the newly formed Arts Council: the winning works included Going To The Match by LS Lowry, with its crowds flocking to Bolton Wanderers’ then home ground, Burnden Park.
An exhibition of the submissions, Football and The Fine Arts, toured the country and the FA secretary, Sir Stanley Rous, said he hoped it would finally break the barrier between those two worlds.
